Commentary.Commentary: What can we expect post Lunch? The pitch has already started to crumble and do not be surprised, if the Windies lose wickets quickly. On the flip side, if the tourists manage to get around 150 runs today and then try and reach upto 200 tomorrow, we could have a game on our hands. Join us back at 1225 local (0655 GMT).

India will be disappointed, to say the least. They had two overnight batsmen, then two more in Ashwin and Jadeja to follow. They would have targetted 400 at least but that last wicket stand gives them something to smile. Now a lead of 56, could have been around 30. In a one-inning shootout, every run is priceless. Credit to Ashwin for hanging in there and not throwing it away. Bigger credit to Thakur and the team management for taking the decision to bat.

Jason Holder was clearly the pick of the bowlers, with a 5-fer but the Windies clearly missed Kemar Roach. The decision to pick Jomel Warrican ahead of the in-form Roach has backfired big time and the tourists will hope that the left-arm spinner does better in the final innings. Gabriel picked up three but was nowhere near his best.

The hosts started the day confidently but then suddenly encountered a nightmare in Jason Holder. He took charge of the second new ball and removed Rahane and Jadeja in quick succession, before Gabriel accounted for Pant. All these without giving away too much runs. The visitors then kept taking wickets and had India on the mat, before Ashwin and Thakur provided a 28-run resistance.

India will smile a bit on the last wicket fightback but overall, it has been Windies' session. They were probably staring at a lead of 100-150 overnight but this morning, they bowled with venom and have restricted the hosts to a lead of 56. The fielding was excellent as well.

OUT! The middle stump is out of the ground. Gabriel ends India's resistance. A length ball just outside off, Ashwin looks to defend but the cherry lands on a crack and then zoots in. Past the bat and crash. INDIA GET A LEAD OF 56!
That bounced. On a length outside off, Ashwin looks to defend but the ball rises steeply and hits the bat on the handle. Ashwin felt the jarring on the impact and immediately took his right hand off.

FOUR! Easy runs. A full toss, on middle, Ashwin just clips it through mid-wicket. There are two men in the deep - at square leg and mid-wicket. However, Shimron Hetmyer at the latter position runs around the ball, instead of across it and ends up chasing it, instead of cutting it off.
Full and outside off, Ashwin comes forward to defend but gets squared up. The ball runs off the outside edge behind point towards third man. They do not run.
Full and on middle, well played by Thakur back to Bishoo.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers. Ashwin wants a run but then changes his mind.
Another long hop, punched towards long on and this time they run.
Quicker one, helped towards short mid-wicket.
A short ball, punched towards long on. No run again.
Tossed up around middle, Ashwin lunges and works it to the leg side.
A length ball around off, helped towards deep backward square leg for a single. Ashwin moves to 30. Excellent knock under pressure.
Full and straight, RA misses his flick and gets hit on the pads. Gabriel puts in an appeal but it is turned down because it is going down. The ball, that is.
Another bouncer, this is ducked under.

TOP EDGE, FOUR! INDIA'S LEAD TOUCHES 50! This last wicket stand is worth 22 from 31 balls. Crucial, useful runs. Not Gabriel's mistake at all. He tests Ashwin with a bouncer and cramps him for room. The batsman goes for the pull but gets a top edge through fine leg which bounces just before the ropes.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Lazy from Jomel Warrican. A short ball outside off, Ashwin punches this through the covers. Should have been just a single, but Warrican takes his own sweet time from long off, gets to the ball, then slides and gets up taking a lot of time. Enough to ensure that India hobble back for the second.

A short ball, on middle, Thakur pulls it with one hand towards deep mid-wicket. Jomel Warrican in the deep had to cover some distance to his left but India do not run. Probably Ashwin thought they did not have enough time to get two. So a dot ball.
Comes down the track and pushes the ball towards mid on. Takes a quick single, makes it easily at the bowler's end but poor Shardul has to test his weak hamstring. Just about makes it.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! VIOLENCE! Dragged short, Ashwin pulls it behind square leg and gets a boundary!
Around off, defended from the crease.
Devendra Bishoo is given an opportunity now. 19-4-72-0 so far.

TOP EDGE, SAFE! Could have been a run out too! Luck is with India and Ashwin at the moment. A short ball, around off, Ashwin looks to pull but gets a top edge as he is cramped for room again. However, such is his luck that the edge is so limp, that Shimron Hetmyer cannot get to it even from short mid-wicket! He misfields too, which allows Thakur to limp across. Had Hetmyer fielded it properly, India would have been bowled out with a run out at the striker's end.

FOUR! Deft guide! Not a bad shot from Ashwin at all. The ball is on a length outside off and it comes in, cramping him slightly for room. But great presence of mind from the all-rounder to realize that the ball is not bouncing much. Just opens the face of the bat and guides it over gully to third man! Gabriel smiles. The stand moves to 10 now.
The field comes in now.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off. Again, they do not run.
A short ball outside off, coming in. Ashwin looks to pull but misses.
Full and outside off, RA drives it towards sweeper cover but does not run.
On a length outside off, Ashwin comes forward and defends.

Okay. So Windies will not be batting in this session, given that 10 minutes are left. However, if the last wicket is not taken by 1130 local, then Lunch will be extended by half an hour. Here is Shannon Gabriel. 18-1-91-2 so far.
Full and around off, pushed towards the bowler.
IN THE AIR... BUT WIDE! Full and wide outside off, nicely tossed up, Ashwin reaches out and looks to drive. He spoons it in the air wide of cover and gets a single.
Eased through mid-wicket for a run.
A tad short, helped towards mid-wicket.
Full and around off, Ashwin comes down the track and pushes it past the diving bowler towards long on for a run.
Full and around off, Thakur leans and works it wide of mid on for a single.
A big heave-ho. Not sure why. A length ball outside off, RA backs away and swings hard, only to miss.
Around off, coming in, punched towards mid on.

Yes-yes, no-no. On a length around middle, Ashwin pushes it towards long on. He sets off for a single but Shardul has not taken a start. He then starts to limp across and now Ashwin stops, because he is not sure whether Thakur can make it to the other end before the throw comes in. So he sends his partner back.
Full on middle, Ashwin flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, driven towards long off. THEY DO NOT RUN.
Outside off, Thakur looks to defend but the ball comes in, takes the inside edge and goes past the stumps towards fine leg. A single taken.
Short and outside off, crunched through the covers for a single. Gets off the mark.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
Shardul Thakur is the last man in, braving his injury and the heat.

OUT! Caught behind! Warrican has his second. He has been trying endlessly to get batsmen driving and caught behind, and eventually gets one. Slightly short, outside off, Umesh looks to cut but only gets a thick nick behind. Luckily for Windies, that sticks. Jahmar Hamilton almost spills this one too. Ashwin is disappointed. INDIA'S LEAD READS 28.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, Ashwin taps it to the off side. Umesh wants a single but is sent back. The fielder from gully comes charging in and then has a shy at the bowler's end, only to miss. Umesh was in though.

Nearly his 6th! Lucky miss for Ashwin. On a length around off, RA gets across to defend but the ball sneaks in, takes the inside edge, hits the pads and almost hits the stumps! Drops beside them, to his relief.
Much fuller, defended watchfully.
Ahhh... on a length outside off, Ashwin looks to steer it towards third man but is beaten due to the extra bounce. Almost nicked it behind.
On a length, around middle, helped straight to mid-wicket.
Full on middle, almost a yorker, swinging in, well played by Umesh Yadav wide of mid on for a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on for a quick single. Gets off the mark.

Lovely loop! What a change of pace too. Warrican tosses this beautifully, well over the batsman's eyeline, outside off. Umesh's eyes light up, as he looks to play the slog sweep. But the ball is so slow, 65 kph to be precise, that he cannot delay his shot any further and ends up missing it altogether!
Full and just outside off, well defended.
Comes down the track and flicks it through mid-wicket for a single.
Around off, spinning away, a touch short, punched towards mid on.
Okay... the camera pans on Shardul Thakur. He is padded up, which means that he will come out to bat if and when the 9th wicket falls.
Full and straight, well kept out by UY, towards mid on.
Similar ball, this time there is not much movement, though Yadav did not play at this one either.
Extensive movement! Full and outside off, Umesh comes forward but then lets the ball go. However, the ball swings a long way further to the off side.
Around off and outside off, Ash pushes it behind point and gets a single. Moves to 10.
Around off, well blocked out.
Full and outside off, hint of outswing, Ashwin covers the line nicely and pushes the ball to cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, Umesh blasts this through the covers but cannot get past the mountain called Jason Holder.
FINALLY A RUN AFTER 29 BALLS! The crowd cheers that. The Windies have tied up the runs so anything added to the score is applauded. Around middle, a tad short, helped towards mid-wicket for a single.
Full again, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, played towards point.
Around middle, defended to the leg side. FOURTH MAIDEN IN A ROW.
On a length around off, watchfully pushed towards cover.
One Yadav replaces another. Umesh comes out at number 10, replacing Kuldeep.

OUT! Lock, stock and barrel! Holder has five! The good morning continues to get better for the Windies skipper. This is real fast bowling, on a not-so-fast pitch. Holder maintains his line outside off and the length is good as well. Kuldeep looks to defend, thinking that he has covered the line but to his dismay, the ball jags back in off the seam. Beats the bat, beats the pad but does not beat the stumps. Uproots the off stump as if a missile has struck. Terrific. 5th 5-wicket haul in Tests for Holder, 4th in 2018!
Back of a length delivery around off, Kuldeep looks to force it through the off side but is done in by the bounce. The ball rolls off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On a length around off, defended watchfully.
Puts his dancing shoes on but cannot quite meet the pitch of the ball. Another block. THIRD MAIDEN ON THE TROT.
Full and around off again, well blocked out.
Short and wide outside off, cut straight to point.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
Around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, eased towards cover.
Beaten! Holder is unlucky in this over. Could have got Kuldeep multiple times. On a length outside off, moving away at the last moment, Kuldeep feels for it and misses.
Outside off, played straight to point.
On a length, around middle, coming in, KY misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.
This goes the other way. Jason is bowling a dream spell this morning. Full and wide outside off, Yadav looks to push but misses. He is lucky not to have edged it.
Full and just around off, watchfully defended.

Banana swing! Something which my colleague GG will not like. He is suffering from cold, you see. So no bananas for him, though he is ready to have a milkshake. Anyways, coming to the ball. Holder comes from around the wicket and bowls a fuller length outside off. The ball curls a long way into the left-hander, though Kuldeep watches it till the last moment and blocks. Strangely, only Holder has been able to extract any movement so far.

Drinks break. Probably the best start Windies could have asked for this morning. Have picked up 3 wickets via Jason Holder (2) and Shannon Gabriel (1) to make their way back in this contest. Still plenty left, mind. Ashwin is out there with Kuldeep and the pair can bat. The Indians will be looking to get a lead around 50-60 runs. Will this partnership add valuable runs or will the tourists wrap the home side up before the end of the session? Also, Jason Holder is back into the attack.
Oooh! Close. Ashwin survives again. Loopy and fuller outside off, he gets a leading edge which goes aerially towards covers. Falls short of the fielder there though and Ashwin survives.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Takes a big stride forward and pushes it back down the track.
Tossed up, slower through the air, the batsman just checks his push and it pops into the air to the bowler's left. Luckily for him, it falls safely.
Turning away from around off, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Sliding in with the angle, Ashwin defends it down on the leg side.
Full ball angling away around off, dug out in front of covers.
Bumper around leg which is too high for Kuldeep to even consider playing at. He ducks and Hamilton behind can't collect on the first attempt, but does well not to concede a run.
Does well to move inside the line and work this neatly through backward square leg. The man in the deep mops it up as the batsmen take one.
Short of a length outside off, rising even more, Ashwin flashes at it and misses.
Second slip comes out and moves to deep mid-wicket.
Angling in on middle and leg, nudged to mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! Gabriel pitches this right up and Kuldeep is expecting this. He drives it through the gap in the covers. Warrican chases it down and tries to pull it back in with a slide, but it seems he can't as he his foot his touching the rope while doing so. Replays confirm the same. Boundary signalled.
Pushed away to the cover fielder off the front foot to end the over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Touch quicker through the air, on off stump, Ashwin stays within his crease to push it out.
Comes forward to this floated ball and meets it with the full face of the bat.
Drifting in from around off, blocked off the front foot.
Tossed up from around the wicket, outside off, eased away to the packed cover region.
Jomel Warrican into the attack for the first time today.
The batsman has played it fine down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Tad short, on middle, a half-whip, half-pull from Ashwin through mid-wicket sees him get a couple of runs.
Fuller on off, tapped down in front of covers. Both batsmen take off and complete the run with ease.
Good movement from Gabriel. Angles it in at first and then makes it go away late, Kuldeep plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Around the off stick, blocked safely from inside the crease.
Three slips in place, along with a gully, for Kuldeep.
Short outside off, Kuldeep tries to have a tame poke at it but fails to make connection.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Too straight in line, easy enough for Ravi Ash to flick it through backward square leg for a double.
Good length ball on the sixth stump line, Ashwin leaves. Has to bring it in just a little bit closer.
Stays on the back foot and keeps it out.
Marginally ahead of a length around off, Ashwin comes half-forward to meet it with a defensive blade.
Shortish delivery on middle, Ashwin uses the angle and works it square on the leg side.

Serves this on a good length this time, keeps it around that off stump channel, Kuldeep blocks. This is the much improved performance from the Windies seamers, have bowled better in the 6 overs this morning than they did all day on Day 2.
Back of a length on off, blocked with the full face of the bat.
Bumper on off, deviating in the air. Goes away slightly and beats the outside edge of Kuldeep's hanging bat.
Kuldeep Yadav walks into the middle next. A short leg is in place for him.

OUT! What a superb catch! Rishabh Pant is dismissed for 92, missing out on a hundred again. Oh, dear. How unfortunate for him. Gabriel pounds it in short outside off and Pant rises to punch this aerially on the off side. Can't keep it down and the placement isn't as good as he would have expected. A bit too close to Hetmyer, who still has a lot of work to do. He moves to his right swiftly and takes an excellent diving catch. Windies back in this game. They'll look to clean the tail up ASAP now.
Short ball on off, blocked right under his eye-line.
Fraction straight in line, on a back of a length, nudged in front of square leg for an easy run. Pant, who's into the 90s, comes on strike.
On the shorter side of things again, blocked down firmly in front of covers.
Hits the deck hard and bangs it in short, Pant defends it down in front of covers and wants the run. Too risky, so Ashwin rightly sends him back.
Ashwin is off the mark as he works this length ball angling into him square on the leg side and takes a single.
Fires it full on this occasion, driven to mid on with a straight bat.
Short of a good length around off, kept out safely off the back foot.
From around the wicket, it's swinging in on a full length, on the stumps, Pant flicks it through towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
A length ball around middle, helped through square leg for a single.
A bouncer outside off, Rishabh sways away from the line.
Full and around off, Pant looks to drive through the on side but the ball swings in a touch and goes off the inner half of the bat. Races across the turf and meets the mid-wicket fence.
Half volley wide outside off, driven straight to cover.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
A length ball wide outside off, left alone. Superb over - W 0 W 0 0 0.

NOT OUT! UMPIRE'S CALL! Ashwin has been saved by a hair's breadth. Holder nearly had three in the over. The second new ball is talking. On a length outside off, Ashwin gets across, looking to tuck but the cherry moves in a long way and misses the bat, hitting the pad. Holder appeals, umpire Ian Gould thinks for a while but then shakes his head. He is dejected a touch, has a chat with his mates and then goes for the review. Umpire's call shows Hawk Eye when it comes to hitting the stumps. Same as Jadeja. Both batsmen could have been given out. Both could have been given not out. Of course, if Jadeja had been given not out, then Ashwin would not have faced this ball at all... just going through the motions.
Review taken. Ashwin has been adjudged not out by umpire Ian Gould, but Holder reckons it is LBW. Is it missing leg?
Outside off on a good length, left alone by Ashwin.
Ravichandran Ashwin is in next to bat.

OUT! GONE! Second of the over for Holder and he's on fire here. The new ball working wonders for him and Windies. What a start for them. Once again pitches it outside off and it swings in a long way, Jadeja without much foot movement looks to defend it from the front foot but is caught flush in front of the stumps. A loud appeal and the finger goes up without wasting any time. India in a spot of bother now.
Appreciable movement from Holder. Lands it outside off and it comes back in a long way, Jadeja covers the line and lets it be.
Ravindra Jadeja is the next batsman in.

OUT! GONE! Will you look at that? A much better line with the new ball and Jason Holder reaps the benefits. Back of a length delivery around off which shoots off the deck, Rahane is taken by surprise and awkwardly fends it away. It goes off the outer half and flies straight to Hope at gully. Rahane is asked to wait for a second to see if the Windies captain overstepped his line and replays show he's fine. So a fine knock from Rahane comes to an end.
Rahane has been caught. The umpires though are checking for the front foot no ball, to nobody's surprise.
Switches the angle again, length ball on off and it's defended well by Pant right beside him.
Short of a good length outside off, Rahane gets on top of the bounce and punches it to deep point. Single to the total.

Over the wicket now. Width on offer, Rahane cuts this fiercely but it's fine stop from Shai Hope at short third man. The placement wasn't as good, a bit too close to him, but it came at him fast. He reacted well to his right to make a stop.
Touch fullish outside off, pushed into the covers for a single.
Rising from a good length, on off, gets more meat on it as he defends it down on the leg side.
Comes from around the wicket and angles in a back of a length delivery on middle and off, Pant looks to play at it but gets an inside edge back onto the box.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end and share the second new ball.
Down the leg side on this occasion, Rahane looks to flick but misses. A wasted over with the new ball in all honesty. Holder needs to do better.
On the sixth stump line, no way Ajinkya will have anything to do with that.
Behind a length, close to off, it's safely kept out off the back foot.
Coming in at first and then shaping away, around off, Rahane stays behind the line and defends.

FOUR! First runs of the morning. Fuller in length and outside off, Rahane takes a step forward and plays a punchy-drive through the covers. The fielders give it a chase, but can't get to it in time. The stand moves to 150 with that and also, India are in the lead.
Too straight in line as Holder sprays it on the pads, Rahane flicks it straight to mid-wicket.
Not surprising. THE SECOND NEW BALL HAS BEEN TAKEN STRAIGHTAWAY. Jason Holder to make the first use of it. Rahane to face. Let's play!
The Windies get into a customary huddle. No Shane Dowrich still, as we see Jahmar Hamilton ready with his keeping gloves. Out come the overnight batsmen - Rishabh Pant and Ajinkya Rahane.

The away side was no clinical enough, but it did have its moments. Managed to wickets at regular intervals, before the huge (unbeaten) Rahane-Pant stand. Spin kept a check on the leaking, will pace back it up though? A lot rides on it. A couple of early wickets this morning could swing the tide in their favour. We'll see how things unfold.

The tie still lies very much in the balance. You could say India are ahead at the moment, but one or two more wickets could change the complexion of the game. The Windies weren't very good with the ball and in the field, to say the least, on Day 2. Some lacklustre displays on their part has seen the hosts come close to the total they posted on the board. Will they manage to take a big lead today? We shall find out. Hello and welcome, folks, for what should be another entertaining day of Test cricket.
... Day 3, First Session ...

Right then! The game has moved ahead slightly. India still in a good position to take a lead close to 100 on Sunday but considering that it is a Day 3 pitch, you can never rule out explosions. If India are restricted to 350, we might be in for a one-inning shootout. Join us at 0930 local (0400 GMT) for all the action. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

The young opener says he was just trying to play his natural game but couldn't convert it into a big one. Adds he enjoyed it though and it was a good batting surface. States that from U-16 level he's been trying to play the ball on its merit, which is his strength. Stresses that he does not want to get confused by thinking too much and intends to continue playing the way he is. Reckons that Gabriel and Holder were bowling quickly, so he just tried to use their pace and find the gaps as best as he could. On his dismissal, he informs that he was just trying to hit it to the left of the cover fielder but the ball was a little away from him, so he couldn't control it. Wants to learn from that and not repeat the same mistake again. Ends by mentioning that it (his dismissal) was a silly shot, so he won't be repeating it in his next innings.

Earlier in the day, Roston Chase managed to get his century but could not quite add much with the tail. Prithvi Shaw then set the stadium alight with a blitzkrieg 70 from just 53 balls. He looked to get consecutive centuries but one false shot brought about his downfall. This is what he has to say as Sanjay Manjrekar has a chat with him.

The Windies had their chances. They had India in a spot of bother at 162/4 with Kohli gone but then fluffed a simple chance offered by Pant. The result was toil and more toil. Jason Holder was the pick of the bowlers with 2/45 while the rest lost the plot during the Pant-Rahane stand.

Pant and Rahane started the final session cautiously but as the period progressed, the former started to get into his own. In a partnership of 146, the southpaw has scored 85. 135 runs came in the final session in 34 overs. The wicketkeeper batsman was in particular, hard on the bowling while Rahane was just content in blocking and milking the bowling.
Superb stuff from India. They have showed why they are such a great force to reckon with. The main in-form batsmen were dismissed around Tea time but then we witnessed a stunning fightback.
A full toss outside off, RP drives it crisply but straight to mid off. STUMPS ON DAY 2, INDIA TRAIL BY 3!
On a length on middle, blocked back to the bowler.
Wide outside off, fuller in length, tempting the drive but Rishabh restrains and shoulders his arms.
Fuller in length, in line of the stumps, pressed towards short mid-wicket.
NO BALL. This is not for overstepping but because Gabriel's back leg was cutting the return crease. Superb call from Bruce Oxenford. Around middle and off, on a length, solidly defended.
Where did that come from? A rare jaffa. Full and outside off, Pant comes forward to defend but at the last moment, the ball pitches and moves away to beat the outside edge!
Outside off, tapped towards cover for a single.
Final over of the day then. The second new ball is available. Will the Windies take it? Not immediately.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Around middle, a tad short, blocked.
Similar ball, eased down to long off for a single.
Full and just outside off, pushed back again. 9 balls left in the day...
Full and around middle, pushed back to the bowler.
A short ball down the leg side, Pant looks to pull but does not go full-heartedly. His bottom hand comes off the bat and he misses.
Kraigg Brathwaite gets a change of ends.
Going for the reverse, gets it to tail in late, bowls it pretty full, around off, but Rahane flicks it towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, watchfully blocked out.
Full and just outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pressed behind point for a run.
Around off, helped to the leg side for a single.
A length ball just outside off, dabbed on the bounce to the keeper.

Surprising. Shannon Gabriel comes back. 11-1-69-1 so far. Don't think the second new ball will be taken because just 3 overs are left today. Meanwhile, we finally get an update on Shane Dowrich - his left knee is just bruised, no bones are broken. So we could see him tomorrow on the field.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and around off, well defended. 19 balls left in the day.
A touch short, on middle, helped through mid-wicket for a single. The deficit is now in single digits.
A touch short, defended to the leg side.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point.
Full and outside off, Rahane dead-bats it.
Full and on the pads, helped through mid-wicket for one.
Thrown a bit wider outside off, Rishabh reaches out and drives it through point for a single to bring up the 300 FOR INDIA. Just 11 adrift now.
Full and just outside off, well blocked out.
The batsman works it down the leg side. One run added to the total. Moves to 70.
Sensible batting. A touch short outside off, punched down to long off for a single.
Landed outside off, pushed towards cover. 29 balls left in the day, Pant needs 19. Would be sensible if he chooses Sunday as the century day.
The Windies vice-captain, Kraigg Brathwaite, has been brought on to bowl.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side.
A bit of an issue with Rahane now. He seems to be cramping up. Not much time left for the close. The physio is having a look at him. All set to go now.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
You guys might have noticed but still, our duty to inform you - we have gone into the extra half hour to try and finish the quota of overs. 5 left after this one.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Rahane goes back and cuts it through the covers for a boundary.
Full and just outside off again, well blocked out.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
On middle, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Roston Chase is back on. 7-1-16-0 so far.
Around off, solidly defended.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.

FOUR! Not a bad result for India, but perhaps Pant fans will not like that. A tad short, Rahane goes back and works it through mid-wicket. Square leg and mid-wicket look at each other as to who should go and retrieve and in the end, both go for it. Neither get to it. The stand moves to 130 while the deficit is now 19.
Darted in on middle, a touch short, worked towards square leg again. 39 balls left in the day. Pant needs 20.
Full and on middle, flicked towards square leg.
Short and outside off, cut straight to backward point.
Outside off, this time Rishabh dabs it behind point for a couple. Moves to 80 from 102 balls.
Floated generously outside off, Pant gets a long way across and then defends.
Dropped short, whipped towards deep mid-wicket for huge cheers from the crowd. Because the strike is rotated and Pant will face.
Tossed up a bit, outside off, eased straight to cover.
Similar ball, just the line is around off, pushed towards cover.
Tossed up around middle, Rahane defends with a lunge.
Full and around middle, a compact defense on offer.
A full toss, on middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket who dives and parries it to the bowler. 49 balls left in the day... Pant needs 22...
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

SIX! TONK! This is a much better hit. Boy, he is going for that century today. Warrican has enough courage to toss the ball up and once again, Pant puts his dancing shoes on. This time he gets to the pitch of the ball and swings it over mid-wicket. The deficit is now 26 while the stand is worth 123.

MISTIMED, BUT SIX! Full and around off, Pant gets down and looks to mow. He is not able to get to the pitch of the ball and miscues it. It is high in the air, seems to have got more elevation than distance but just about clears long on.
Tossed up around middle and leg, worked to the mid-wicket region.
Around off, spinning in, Pant gets across and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Shorter than the previous short of fuller length, cut hard to sweeper cover for a single. India just trail by 39 now. Rahane moves to 60 while the stand is worth 110.
A tad short of full, Rahane goes back and defends it watchfully.
Around off, pushed towards cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
A mini Drinks break. There seems to be an issue with one of the stump cameras. All sorted now. Ready to resume. Another 10 overs left in the day.
Tossed up on middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Outside off, coming in, left alone.
Landed outside off, Pant dabs it towards third man, sets off for a run but first slip dives to his left and parries it to backward point. Rahane sends his partner back.
Full and just around off, well defended.
Shorter in length, cut through point for a single.
Landed outside off, a touch short, punched back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside off, Pant covers the line and leaves it alone.
Short, flat and a little close to off, Rahane is a little cramped for room but he still manages to get the cut away to sweeper cover for a single.
Nudges it through towards deep backward square leg and changes ends.
Goes with the spin and defends it down on the leg side.
FOUR! BANG! That's hammered. Tossed up, a lot of flight and Pant is enticed. He gives it the full swing of the bat and beats mid off easily to the fence.
From around the wicket, it's turning in from outside off, Pant blocks from the front foot.
Quick, short and flat on the stumps, Rahane goes deep inside the crease and offers a straight bat in response.
Waits for the ball to come as he uses his wrists to work it away into the leg side. Two runs collected.
Negotiates with the full ball well by coming forward.
Ajinkya remains rock solid in defense as he keeps bat and pad close together to keep it out.
Brings his bat ahead of his pad and safely deal with it.
Full and drifting in on middle and off, Rahane is right behind the line as he defends.
Full and attacking the stumps, driven back to the bowler.
Short and around off, blocked again, this time off the back foot.
Pant takes a huge stride forward and meets the ball with the full face of the bat.
Short and wide outside off, cut to deep point. One more to the total and that brings up the 100-run stand between these two.
Moves across again, gets inside the line and works it behind square leg for a single.
Sharp spin into Rishabh Pant, the southpaw moves across to cover the line and defends.
Looped up around off, driven to mid off to end the over.
Leans into the full ball outside off and pushes it to covers.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Worked away on the leg side. Dot ball.
Full and outside off, driven to the covers.
Quicker one darted on the stumps, blocked with a straight bat.
Rahane adjusts inside the crease and pulls the short ball through square leg. Three runs taken.
Short, flat and turning in from outside off, forces it through cover-point. One run collected.
Takes a stride forward and dead-bats it into the track.
Goes square as Rishabh punches it firmly square through covers. Ambris covers good ground from deep point and keeps the batsmen down to two.
Too straight in line, flicked through square leg for a run.
Goes with the spin as he wrists it through mid on for one.
Tossed up and turning in outside off, Pant wildly slogs it down to long on. Didn't middle it, but will get the single either way.
Hangs back and keeps it out off the back foot.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. Won't get any run for it.
Spinning in, on middle and leg, Pant goes back and works it down on the leg side.
Keeps it on off this time, driven to mid off.
Full and straight outside off, pushed gently into the covers.
Drills this very full ball in line of the stumps to long on and jogs across to the other end. The hosts trail by 60 runs.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have picked up a couple of runs. The 250 comes up for India.

And now Pant follows. Gets to this 2nd fifty in Test cricket comfortably. He goes back to the ball spinning into him and turns it through to deep backward square leg for a double. A fine knock from the youngster as well.

15th Test fifty for Ajinkya Rahane! It's been a patient knock from the Indian vice captain. Well-deserved. He opens the face and dabs it behind square on the off side to complete his half century. Wonderful knock so far.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Nice shape on that. Tossed up leg spinner on off, blocked from the front foot.
Final official Drinks break of the day.
Backs away to this shortish ball and punches it a bit square towards sweeper cover. Single to keep strike.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Floats it up there, in line of the stumps, Pant with a drive finds mid on.
Hangs back and keeps it out off the back foot.
Pant comes forward to this tossed up ball and defends it away safely.
Sliding in on middle and leg, Ajinkya moves inside the line and works it away behind square on the leg side. Single taken.
Jomel Warrican back on.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
That must have stung. Even Rahane is laughing. Short ball which comes rather slowly, Rahane is into the pull shot too early and wears it on the body. Rubs the area instantly and laughs it off.
Quicker one outside off, forced into the off side for one.

FOUR! Beautiful placement from Rishabh Pant. Tossed right up there on middle, Pant gets low, rolls his wrists over the ball and sweeps it wide of short fine leg. It races away to the fence for a boundary.
Turning away from a shorter length this time, cut to sweeper cover for a single.
Quite slow through the air around off, blocked off the front foot.
Switches the angle to around the wicket and angles in a back of a length ball close to off, Pant stays behind and defends it down on the off side.
Back of a length outside off, Rahane taps it down in front of point and both batsmen take off. Complete the run with ease too. Nicely done.
FOUR! Easy runs. On the pads and all Ajinkya Rahane to do was get something on it. He did and the ball raced away to the fine leg boundary.
Comes wide of the crease and angles it in on off, Rahane brings down a straight blade to defend under his nose.
Too far outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
Length delivery darted on middle and off, angling in, played off the inner half in front of square leg. Dot ball.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

UPPISH, SHORT AND FOUR! Hetmyer is the fielder. Full and outside off, Pant gets down and mows the slog sweep. Initially, it seems like Shimron Hetmyer at long on has a chance but the ball dips on him and in the end, he is not able to get to the ball. Worse, it slips past him to the fence behind.
FOUR! Cheeky! Landed outside off, Pant waits for the ball to come to him and dabs it past backward point!
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Another issue with the ball. Holder is not happy with the shape, nor is Bishoo. Umpire Ian Gould has a look at it, but then cuts of a thread and then the game resumes.
Full on middle, pushed towards long on for a single.
Devendra Bishoo is back on. 11-4-28-0 so far.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Another fine piece of fielding. A short ball again, pulled towards deep square leg where a diving effort keeps the batsmen to two.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Though this time, the fielder is not at fault. Full and outside off, Rahane punches it down the ground, just past the stumps at the other end. Roston Chase slides from mid on to his left but at the last moment, just when the slide comes, the ball bounces over his hands!
Excellent fielding. Short and outside off, Rahane punches it towards deep point. Substitute Keemo Paul chases it to his right and dives full stretch to prevent the boundary. Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Short and outside off, Rahane waits for the ball to come to him and then guides it towards point where Roston Chase does well.
Driven through the covers by the batsman.

MISFIELD, FOUR! Short and outside off, Pant cuts it straight to point who simply does not get behind the line of the ball. It goes through and it is a boundary. 50-RUN STAND IS UP. The deficit is now down to double figures.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Comes down the track and pushes it back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Full and outside off, well blocked out.
On a length outside off, Jinx walks across and looks to tuck but misses and is hit on the pads. The ball deflects towards fine leg and a leg bye is taken.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Another bouncer, down the leg side, ducked under.
NO BALL. Well, Gabriel has overstepped by a massive margin. A short ball, outside off, cutting in, Ajinkya looks to pull but misses.
A short ball wide outside off, Rahane lets it go.
Short and outside off, punched through point for a run. Now Rahane gets into the 30s.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. Moves to 30 from 49 balls.
Around off, well defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full again, outside off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, Rahane works it through mid-wicket for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Down the leg side, flicked fine for a run.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot for a single.

EDGED, DROPPED, FOUR! Poor keeping from the substitute and the Indian wicket-keeper batsman gets a life. Short and wide outside off, Pant throws his bat at it but the feet do not move much. As a result, he gets a thick outside edge. Jahmar Hamilton, the stand-in keeper for Shane Dowrich, makes half an attempt to his left but the ball bursts through his gloves to the third man fence. Poor Gabriel... Meanwhile, 200 comes up for India.
On a length outside off, pushed towards cover.
Short and wide outside off, slapped to deep point for a single.
Shannon Gabriel is back on. 7-1-48-1 so far.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Full and just outside off, well blocked out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Around middle, helped through square leg for a single.
Comes forward and pushes it towards short mid-wicket.
Full and around middle, turned towards short fine leg.
Outside off, let through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and miles outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Fine shot. Down the leg side, Pant flicks this uppishly behind square leg and gets a boundary! The stand is worth 32 while the deficit is down to 117.
A huge appeal for a caught behind, but nothing in it. Full and down the leg side, Pant looks to flick but misses.

A length ball outside off, comes in a long way, Pant shoulders arms and is hit on the thigh pads. The ball deflects to the leg side and Pant wants the single but then realizes that one cannot run when he has been hit on the pads while not offering a shot.
The batsman has played it towards mid-wicket.
Full on middle, flicked towards short mid-wicket.
Driven towards the mid off region. One run added to the total.
Landed outside off, let through.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and outside off, cut straight to point.

FOUR OVERTHROWS, FIVE RUNS IN TOTAL! The crowd goes wild. In a period where runs have come in a trickle, this is a welcome bonus. Full and outside off, Pant pushes it wide of mid off and goes for a quick single. Roston Chase hurries to his right and has a wild throw at the bowler's end. The backup is at mid-wicket and by the time he can get across, the ball is past him in a flash to the boundary behind.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended towards the off side.
Landed outside off, RP defends solidly.
Full and outside off, Rishabh reaches out and meets the ball to drive towards cover.
On a length outside off, Pant walks across to defend but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Full and well outside off, left alone.
Pushes this through mid on and keeps the strike for the next over.
Full and just around off, well kept out.

FOUR! THWACK! That is the way he plays. Full and wide outside off, Pant reaches out and crashes it wide of long off for a boundary! The deficit is now 128. Pant moves to 13 from 20 balls with his third boundary while the stand is worth 21.
Tossed up wide outside off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around middle, Pant lunges and defends.
FOUR! Flashed and flashed hard! No stopping this one. Short and wide outside off, Rahane throws his bat at that and gets it over gully to the third man fence!

Full and down the leg side, Rahane tickles it towards fine leg. The ball races away to the fence but Devendra Bishoo races across to his right and dives full length to pull the ball back in. Two runs taken or saved - whichever team you are supporting or looking at.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
On a length outside off, played towards point.
Here's Jason Holder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Landed outside off, left alone.
A bit fuller again, driven straight to cover.
Outside off, bowled slowly through the air, Pant waits for the ball to come to him and then dabs it towards point. Wants a single but is sent back.
This is a bit wide outside off, full again, driven hard but straight to cover.
Full and outside off, slow turn, left alone.

The Windies get into a huddle. They look to be pumped up but then lazily spread out. Out come Rahane and Pant. Roston Chase to open the attack for the session. He did that post Lunch too. Pant on strike. Here we go!
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

India are not behind by much, but they just need to be a bit more careful here. This pitch is such that a wicket could lead to a couple more and if the Windies manage to break the Rahane-Pant stand quickly, they could suddenly start thinking about the lead. On the flip side, if Pant gets going, that deficit could come down pretty quickly. Batting in the second innings is not going to be easy at all. Stay tuned for the final session, where 34 overs are scheduled to be bowled.

Excellent bowling from Jomel Warrican in particular. He managed to get the big wicket of Prithvi Shaw and then, stifled the scoring. Bishoo has been equally economical, with figures of 11-4-28-0. So the plan from the Windies is quite clear - dry out the runs and induce mistakes from the batsmen.

The session started with Prithvi Shaw resuming his run-scoring panache but once he was dismissed, the visitors found their way back into the game a bit. They dried out the runs, got a few maiden overs on the trot and then, just before Tea, Holder managed to nip out his counterpart.

Well, the session figures read 93 runs in 31 overs for three wickets but we can split that into two halves. 53 runs came in 14 overs till the Drinks break but after that, it has been a real struggle to score runs. The Windies have been disciplined and economical and as a result, eked out a few wickets.
A wide ball outside off to end the session, left alone. TEA ON DAY 2, INDIA TRAIL BY 138!
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Out of nowhere! A short ball outside off, Rahane looks to fend but suddenly, the cherry shoots up, hits the batsman onto his gloves and then on his helmet. Drops down in front of first slip though.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Outside off, punched towards mid off where Shannon Gabriel puts in a desperate dive to his left to stop the ball.
Full and outside off, left alone.
This could be the last over before Tea...

SAFE. The foot was in the air but it came down before the bails could be dislodged. Pant ran down the track but Bishoo smartly bowled a leg spinner, slightly wider than the batsman would have anticipated. Rishabh is beaten in the flight but he does one thing correctly - does not go through with his shot, just tries to defend. As a result, he gets time to drag his foot back in. Substitute Jahmar Hamilton is not the quickest. After it is referred upstairs, there is a bit of an issue with the overstepping but a closer look indicates that the ball is fine.
Is that a stumping? Pant looks to be home... referred upstairs...

FOUR! Nicely done! Slightly short outside off, Pant waits for the ball to come to him and then deftly guides it past gully to the third man fence! The stand is worth 11 and the deficit is down to 138.
Around off, Pant stays back and defends.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside leg, watchfully defended
Short and outside off, cut through point for a single.
Shaping back in from around the wicket, on a length, Pant off the inner half plays it back in the bowler's direction.
Angling back in on middle and leg, goes off Jinx's pads as he misses his flick. A leg bye is taken.
Served in the channel outside off, left alone by the right-hander.
Dabbed through cover-point. A length ball is placed well and a single is to be had.
Fired full outside off, Pant squeezes it out on the bounce to gully.

FOUR! Played that with soft hands, which was the key. Length delivery outside off from around the wicket, Pant leans ahead and with a slightly opened face places it between the slip cordon and gully for a boundary.
Goes deep inside the crease and pushes it away from danger.
Comes well forward and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Short and flat on the stumps, blocked off the back foot.
Full again, outside off, pushed away defensively on the off side.
Looped up leg break outside off, Rahane lunges forward to defend.
From around the wicket to Pant, Holder pitches it outside off, it's left alone. A successful over from the Windies skipper comes to an end.
Rishabh Pant to bat next.

OUT! It's umpire's call and the on-field decision stays. Jason Holder gets the big fish after bringing himself back into the attack. This length delivery cuts back in and catches Kohli on the front pad. Loud shout and the finger goes up. Virat, after speaking with his partner, takes the review. It goes upstairs and replays show the ball to be clipping the leg stump. So, he's gone. Timely strike for the tourists.
The DRS has been taken. Big moment in the game as Virat Kohli is caught leg before. Height is the only thing that can save him. Maybe missing leg? Let's see...
Darts the full ball on middle, Kohli once again finds mid on with a drive.
Full ball attacking the stumps, driven to the man at mid on.
Angling in on leg, VK picks it off his pads and clips it behind square leg for a couple of runs.
Seaming away off the deck from a length, Kohli runs it down to short third man.
Pushed away on the back foot on the off side.
Uses the depth of the crease to go back and wrist it in front of square leg for a single.
Some attacking intent as Rahane skips out to meet the ball at its pitch. Works it to the right of mid on at the edge of the ring and takes a run.
Tossed up this time, Rahane dead-bats this.
Slightly shorter in line of the stumps, Ajinkya is on the back foot as he defends it.
Too straight in line, flicked away through to deep square leg. One run collected.
Picks it off his pads and turns it away on the leg side for a single.
Goes square this time. Opens the face to this length ball outside off and dabs it in front of point.
Full in length outside off, the Indian skipper makes sweet connection on the cover drive but can't get it past the fielder.
Kohli defends this length ball by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fraction straight in line, wristed through the vacant spaces in the mid-wicket region for a double.
Length delivery shaping in from outside off, Virat remains inside his crease and blocks it right beside him.
Jason Holder back on.
Full on the stumps, defended to end the over.
The batsman has played it to the point region. Won't get any run for it.
Once more, dances down the track and blocks.
Makes good use of the feet to get close to the pitch and then defends it out.
Floated up around the off stick, met with the full face of the bat.
Turning away from around off, driven to the cover fielder.
Angling in on middle and leg, Kohli uses the angle to flick it to mid-wicket.
Coming in on middle, driven to mid on.
Dropped short and outside off, Rahane chops the cut wide of point. One run to the total.
Drifting in from around off, met with a straight blade in defense.
Minimal foot movement, but it's enough to get close to the pitch and defend.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Angling down from leg stump, catches the batsman on the pads.

FOUR! The 50-run stand is up with this. A misfield helps with that. Virat Kohli goes on the back foot and whips it to mid on. Keemo Paul (sub) moves to his right to stop it but it goes through him. A boundary results.
Moves inside the line and works it away on the leg side for a single.
Pushes this full delivery right back at the leggie.
Full on the stumps, defended right under the eye-line.
Short and wide outside off, punched square on the off side for one.
Full and in line of the stumps, defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Keeps it full, Rahane blocks it off the front foot.
Full and angling in on middle and leg, wristed wide of mid on for a single.
Quicker one on off, takes the inside edge onto the pads.
Slower through the air on off, met with a defensive blade in response.
Defended off the front foot by Rahane presenting the full face of the bat.
Hangs back inside the crease and pats it away to safety.
Pushed away to the cover region. No run taken.
Spinning away from middle and off, full in length, blocked.
Kohli place this wide of the man at mid off and takes off. Rahane is a bit late to respond but he still makes it well in time.
FOUR! Shot. A shade on the shorter side from Bishoo with a little bit of room as well, Kohli plays this really late as he goes back and cuts it past short third man for a boundary.
Worked just wide of the mid on fielder for a brisk run.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Pushed away with the full face of the bat to the mid off fielder.
Floats it up around off, kept out by coming ahead.
Tossed up just outside off, driven to mid off.
Rahane goes back after seeing the ball landing short and cuts it away through the off side for one run.
FOUR! A boundary after almost 12 overs. It's quite full, so Kohli comes well ahead and hammers this straight back past the bowler to find the fence.
Dabs this to point from within the crease.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full outside off, driven to covers.
Keeps it full once more, blocked away.
A run finally. Short and wide outside off, cut away square on the off side for a single.
Another maiden. Kohli drives to mid off and wants the run, but is sent back just in time.
Uses the angle into him to wrist it to the mid-wicket area.
Meets it with the full face of the bat and blocks.
Comes ahead again with a big stride and keeps it away.
VK has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Drifting in from around off, pushed away on the off side for nothing.
Pushes this full delivery tamely down the track.
Attacking the stumps, Rahane brings his bat ahead of his pads before blocking it out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Very slow through the air, on a driving length around off, left alone after covering the line.
In the gap this time. Through the covers for a run.
Loopy leg break outside off, Kohli drives it straight to the man at cover.
Maiden over from Warrican. Loops it outside off, Rahane withdraws his bat and lets it go.
Defends it from the inner portion in front of mid-wicket.
Make that four in a row. Solidly done from Rahane.
Three similar balls, three identical shots.
Keeps bat and pad close together as he blocks it from the front foot again.
Full ball darted on off stump, Ajinkya Rahane presents a front foot defensive shot.

Drinks are on the field. Best spell of bowling from the Windies. They've managed to pick up a few wickets and are piling the pressure on the Indian batsmen with some tight lines. They'll need to continue in the same vein for longer and hope it brings them a wicket or two more before the end of the session. India need a big partnership, and the two men in the middle are the perfect candidates for the job. This next hour should be interesting.
Full and quick on off, blocked off the front foot. Consecutive maidens for Devendra Bishoo.
Patted away to the same fielder again. Another dot.
Full outside off, driven to covers.
Taps it down in front of covers. Not much turn on offer.
Camps back again, turns it away with in the wrists in front of square leg.
Leg break turning away from middle, Virat uses the depth of the crease to go back and work it down on the leg side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Kohli pushes this towards mid on and is off in an instant. Completes the run quickly as a result.
Stays perfectly behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Shortish again, another defensive shot on offer.
Quick and short on off stump, VK is on the back foot as he blocks it down the track.
Quite slow through the air and the ball grips and turns away off the surface around off, Kohli reaches out to it and pushes it on the off side with an open face.
Quicker one on the stumps, Ajinkya looks to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Keeps bat and pad close together as he guards it out safely.
On the fuller side of things, blocked.
Good effort from Hetmyer, saves vital runs for his side. Rahane drives it to the covers but Shimron makes a good tumbling stop.
Touch short in length, so this time Jinx is on the back foot to defend.
Looped up delivery just around off, defended easily off the front foot.
Good running. Rahane hits this full toss wide of mid off. Both batsmen take off fast and complete the run with ease.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Drifting in, flicked to the man at short mid-wicket.
Comes forward and plays it back to the bowler.
Sliding in on middle and leg, Kohli picks up the half volley and flicks it through mid-wicket for one.
Spinning away from around off, Rahane goes back and slaps the punch to sweeper cover for a single.
Short and outside off, cut through point for one more.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full and outside off, driven straight to short extra cover.
JUST WIDE! A tad short, Rahane goes back and turns it in the air. Manages to evade short mid-wicket. Mid on tracks it down and the batsmen return for the second.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Devendra Bishoo time.
A short ball, around middle, pulled to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Virat looks to flick but gets a leading edge towards cover.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Full and outside off, coming in with the angle, left alone. If you remember, in 2017, in Pune, Kohli had left a ball alone from Steven O'Keefe from Australia. It was a similar arm ball, which just came in and hit the timber. This is well past the off stump.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.

Full and outside off, Virat reaches out, plays it with soft hands behind point, runs the first one really hard, turns back for the second but the fielder is quick to get to the ball. Just the single then.
Full and outside off, Kohli gets forward and across and defends to the off side.
Outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Full and outside off, hint of inswing, Rahane comes forward and pushes it towards mid off.
Outside off, a tap and run towards point. The stand moves to 20 from 19 balls while the deficit is now 189.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
This time he calls for two and gets two. Full on middle, flicked through mid-wicket.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.

MIX-UP, SAFE! A nervy moment for the Indians. Rahane turns it towards mid-wicket and takes the single. Kohli initially calls for the second and Rahane responds. However, the skipper then changes his mind and sends his partner back. Poor Rahane has to dive back in. Luckily for him, the throw is a weak one to the bowler, almost in the middle of the pitch.

IN THE AIR... SAFE!!! If only the man had not been moved to sweeper a ball before. Full and outside off, Rahane looks to drive but cannot control his shot. It is in the air but there is no man catching at cover-point. Easy single to the man in the deep.
FOUR! GLORIOUS! Full toss outside off, Rahane leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! Immediately a man is placed at sweeper cover.
Outside off, pushed wide of mid off for a single. The stand is worth 10 at run-a-ball. The deficit is now 199.
Full and wide outside off again, left alone.
FOUR! GORGEOUS! So good to the eye. Half volley outside off, a touch wide, Kohli leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! His second in 4 balls. Moves to 12 from 10 balls.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and wide outside off, driven wide of mid off for a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
MISFIELD, FOUR! Full on middle, Kohli drives it towards mid on who should have well, stopped it but he puts in a lazy dive. He misses the ball and it is the first boundary for the Indian skipper.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Ajinkya Rahane joins his skipper in the middle, coming in at number 5.

OUT! Caught behind! There you go - one wicket brings another! Big blow by Gabriel. He lands it on a length outside off, but it is wide enough to be left alone. Pujara though, wants to have a poke and gets a thin edge behind, because the footwork is not the greatest. He was reaching for the ball. Substitute keeper Hamilton collects and straightaway appeals. Gabriel does not even bother appealing but someone has, hence the umpire raises his finger! India trail by 209. Have the Windies got an opening?
Full and wide outside off, Kohli reaches out to drive and gets a thick outside edge towards point. The fielder dives to his left and makes a partial stop. A run taken.
Full on middle, Kohli flicks it through mid-wicket. Should have been just a single but a poor throw at the keeper's end makes the batsmen return for the second.
Full and around middle, Pujara is early into the flick and gets a leading edge wide of cover. A single taken. Moves to 10.
Pushes this towards mid on.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has punched that ball through the off side.
Skipper Virat Kohli walks in at number 4, replacing Shaw.

OUT! He has thrown it away! Shaw will be gutted with himself. A loose shot in a nearly flawless innings. Full and outside off, a bit tossed up, a bit wide, Shaw cannot resist and goes hard on the drive. Cannot keep it down and finds Shimron Hetmyer at extra cover. You can look at this shot in two ways - a. Oh Shaw! What have you done? Or b. Well played, Shaw. You have again given India a motoring start. The dressing room stands up and applauds the youngster. How will the Windies be feeling? Relieved to see his back? Or the sense of more pain on seeing who is coming in next? The Indian skipper, that is.
FOUR! FLAMBOYANT! Full and outside off, Shaw leans and drives it wide of mid off for a boundary!
Full on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple.
Jomel Warrican is back on. 6-1-28-0 so far. Is this a change of ends for a bowler or was that Roston Chase over just an experiment?
Full and down the leg side this time, flicked straight to deep mid-wicket for a single. 11 from the over!
FOUR! FANTASTIC! Full and wide outside off, Shaw leans and drives it through the covers. Not a soul moves! The young lad has moved to 63 now, in just 48 balls! 10 fours, 1 six.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
Full and down the leg side, Prithvi misses his flick.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a well-run brace.
FOUR! Smart batting. Very full outside off, almost a yorker, Shaw just squeezes it past second slip towards third man! The deficit is now 226.
Shannon Gabriel to bowl from the other end. 3-1-20-0 so far. Trust me, those 3 overs took a lonngggg time to be bowled.
Another one to the fielder. Around middle, helped towards backward square leg once more.
Fullish on middle, this is flicked to short mid-wicket now.
This is around off, Pujara gets a long way across and flicks - but straight to backward square leg again.
A bit of drift, bowled on the pads, turned towards backward square leg.
Full and around middle, flicked straight to backward square leg.
On the pads, an easy giveaway, a single towards square leg with the flick. The stand moves to 20.

We are back after the Luncheon interval. Will we see any better effort in the field from the Windies? The players are slowly making their way out. Roston Chase will start off things after Lunch. Shaw to face. Here we go!
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

With such an attacking beginning, India now trail by 231. The pitch is starting to play tricks and hence, this sort of cricket could be the best option on this track. Because you never know, a wicket here could trigger a couple more. Join us back at 1210 local (0640 GMT).

Nothing much to talk about the Windies' bowling. The opening over went for 15 runs and that set the tone. It has looked nothing short of listless and the only wicket that they have got has been because of Rahul's misjudgement. They might have had Shaw but right now, Midas has been reborn in the form of the Mumbai lad.

Prithvi Shaw is the man for the future for India. The young genes in him have made his team take the bull by the horns. On a pitch where Rahul was tentative, Pujara has not yet looked free-flowing, this lad is in his zone. Has an array of shots and is displaying those for everyone to see.
What a session for India. Started by Umesh. Finished by Shaw. The Windies might have scored 311 but they look totally downcast at the moment.
Full and around off, watchfully kept out. LUNCH ON DAY 2, INDIA TRAIL BY 231 RUNS!
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Comes down the track and blocks.

FOUR! Superb from Pujara. Great timing. Fractionally short outside off, the right-hander goes back and punches it between cover and point. Devendra Bishoo gives it a good chase from cover but comes second best.
Slow turn, pitched outside off, going away, blocked towards cover.
Full and around off, eased down to long off for a single.
Very full, just outside off, Cheteshwar blocks it towards mid on.
Full and around off, watchfully kept out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length outside off, cuts back in, Pujara looks to defend but is taken aback by the movement. Looks to fend it away but gets an inside edge which drops down to the leg side.
Full and outside off, driven slightly wide of mid off for a single.
On a length around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Comes down the track again and defends.
Comes down the track and drives it straight to cover.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side.

Easily done. A half century in just 39 balls. For the second time in two innings, he has touched the 50-mark. And this has been another innings of dominance. Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single. The dressing room is applauding with plenty of smiles. It has been that sort of a knock.
Full and straight, pushed back to the bowler.
On a length outside off, shouldered arms to.
Full and outside off, Cheteshwar walks into the shot and drives but straight to wide mid off.
A touch wider outside off, Pujara lets it be.
Full and around off, defended watchfully.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, Shaw drives it wide of mid off. Shannon Gabriel puts in a tired effort to his left with a tumble but manages to stop the ball. A single taken.
The batsman dances down the track once more and decides to defend it.
Comes out of his crease again but blocks this time.
FOUR! Good use of the feet from Cheteshwar Pujara. Good shot. Dances down to get close to the pitch and drives it past mid on to send it across the boundary line.
In line of the stumps, met with a defensive bat in response.
Knocks it down the ground to long on for a run.

Dropped! Difficult chance as it comes quite fast at him but in such games you've got to be taking those. Spinning away, short in length, Shaw backs away to cut but the ball bounces a bit more and takes the outside edge. Hope at first slip moves to his left, gets his fingertips to it but can't hold on. A brace results.
Curving away late from around off, on a length, left alone to end the over.
Just ahead of a length on off, blocked down right under his nose.
Better from Holder. Has been quite consistent so far with his lines. Keeps it in that off stump channel, makes it go away as Cheteshwar leaves it alone.
Wide of off again, another leave.
Wide outside off stump, Pujara leaves it alone.
Uses the angle into him and flicks it away through mid-wicket for one run.
Che is watchful as he plants his front foot ahead and meets the tossed up ball with the full face of the bat.
Nicely played. Mid on is pushed back for Prithvi so he just plays it to the man in the deep. Takes a run for doing so.
Quick run. Pujara wrists this just wide of mid on and rushes to the other end.
Slower through the air on off, Pujara strides ahead to keep it out.
Shapes up for the cover drive and places it in the gap for a run.
Short, flat and on the stumps, punched back to the bowler.
Length delivery aiming the top of off stump, Pujara defends it solidly from inside the crease.
Fires it down the leg side, this time Hamilton moves swiftly to his left and catches the ball with a dive.
Cheteshwar Pujara walks in at no.3.

OUT! Rahul's troubles finally come to an end. He wasn't looking as assured as his partner, pays the price for it. Short of a length just outside off, Rahul is in two minds about what to do. He initially wants to play but then decides to leave it late. The ball takes the inside edge and disturbs the bails. First wicket down for India, against the run of play.
Better. Attacks the stumps on this occasion, full in length, Rahul keeps bat and pad close together to keep it out.
Well outside off again, left alone this time.
Width offered outside off, a lot of it, Rahul plays a half-hearted shot and gets beaten on the cut.
Slower through the air on off, blocked by coming well forward.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

FOUR! Make that number 3. Though, this is a result of some poor fielding from the Windies skipper. Shaw drives it to the left of mid off. Holder moves quickly but can't get low to stop the ball. Lets it through to the fence behind.
FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Goes the other side this time. Shaw opens his body up to this flighted delivery and drives it through the covers for another boundary.

FOUR! Takes the aerial route and gets the desired result. Tossed up delivery on off, Shaw decides to take this on. Gets low and slog sweeps it over mid-wicket for a one-bounce boundary. The 50 is up for India with this.
Drifting in from around the wicket, Prithvi clears his front leg and drives it back down. The bowler gets low to his left and parries it towards mid off.
Coming back in on leg, angling further down, catches the pads of the batsman as he fails to play the flick shot.
Rahul has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
No ball! Seems Gabriel's bad habit is catching on to his skipper. Good length ball shaping away around off, Rahul defends it on the off side. Jason overstepped, so no ball signalled.
A little bit of swing away from Shaw, the batsman checks his drive as he places it past the cover fielder. One run taken. The deficit is now 263.
FOUR! Too full, too straight. Shaw moves inside the line and flicks it ever so well through the gap in the mid-wicket area. Beautifully played, no stopping that.
Positions himself perfectly behind the line and blocks.
Back of a length on off, cramping the batsman for room. But young Shaw rocks onto the back foot and punches it square to point.
Change of ends for Jason Holder.
Some drift in again, wristed down towards mid on once more. Can't find the gap.
Drifting in on middle and off, Rahul gets his front leg out of the way and drives it to mid on.
Pushed away in front of covers by coming half-forward.
Similar delivery, similar shot.
Quicker through the air and full outside off, defended easily by coming onto the front foot.
A little too full for his liking, on off, dug out to extra cover by KL.
Jomel Warrican into the attack already. Spin introduced early by the Windies.
FOUR! Inconsistent with the line again and he's paid the price. On the pads, Shaw comfortably flicks it away through backward square leg, beating fine leg who tries to cut it off.
Angles this full ball in on the stumps, worked off the inner half in front of square leg for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Goes fuller this time, keeps it around off, Rahul looks to play the expansive drive but gets an inside edge back onto his pads.

FOUR BYES! More extras. All most of the runs going to come via extra today? Seems like it from the looks of things. Gabriel angles it too far down leg and the keeper has no chance to reach it this time. Across the fine leg fence and that's a boundary.
In the channel outside off, holding its line, KL has nothing to do with that one.
Tight line. On off, a good length ball, blocked with the full face of the bat.

FOUR BYES! Now, after two good ones, a poor effort shows and it's from the substitute keeper. Down the leg side, Hamilton moves to his left but doesn't get to the ball at all when he should have. It runs away to the fence for a boundary.
Decent stop from Ambris. Prithvi Shaw with a superb cover drive, but can't get it past a diving Sunil Ambris who gets low to his right to stop it.
Cutting back in from a good length on off, defended from the back foot down on the off side.

Good effort from Devendra Bishoo. Another good shot from Shaw. He leans ahead and drives the full ball through mid off. Bishoo chases it down well from mid on and pulls it back inside the rope. The batsmen only take two.
FOUR! Shot. As good as they come. Full and swinging away from around off, Shaw opens his body up a bit, along with the bat face, and drives it neatly through cover-point to fine the fence.
Fullish delivery outside off, blocked off the front foot in front of covers.

Dowrich is receiving some medical attention after copping a blow on the previous delivery. Slight halt in play as a result. Bad news for the touring side - their keeper is being taken off the field. Jason Holder and his men will want him to come back soon. Meanwhile, Jahmar Hamilton will take the gloves.

FOUR BYES! That did not rise at all. And it must have stung Shane Dowrich as well. Yikes! Gabriel serves it on a back of a length outside off, Rahul lets it be and the ball keeps really low. Dowrich behind the stumps tries to stop it with his legs but gets struck on the left knee. The ball deflects towards the third man fence for a boundary, but the Windies keeper is down the ground.
Darts it full and well outside off, once more KL defends it but from the inner portion of the bat.
Too far outside off, no shot offered by the batsman.
Full in length outside off, coming back in, Rahul defends it off the inner half back down the track.
Heavy movement for Gabriel. Comes wide of the crease and angles it in from outside off. Rahul leaves but he doesn't expect so much movement. Luckily for the batsman, still well wide of the off stick.
Further away outside off, dabbed straight to point.
Short of a good length close to off, kept out by rising on his toes.
Jason fires it full and it's angling in on leg, catches Shaw low on the pads as he fails to flick it away. No appeal though, it was going down leg.

No ball and FOUR! Full and swinging away from outside off, Shaw reaches out to it and plays it off the outer half between the slip cordon and gully. Away to the fence she goes. No ball also signalled as Holder overstepped on that occasion.
Just ahead of a length, defended by staying right behind the line.
Full delivery first angling in and then shaping away on off, Shaw brings a straight bat down in defense.
Bit of a false start from Holder. Sprays this down the leg side. Shaw looks to flick it fine but fails to make connection.
Jason Holder will share the new ball with Gabriel.

Full and outside off, driven past the sliding bowler down the ground for a quick single. The over finally ends. My colleague could easily go and wash his face, get a cup of coffee and then come and sit. Still, Gabriel was yet to bowl his final ball.
On a length outside off, pushed towards cover.
NO BALL, SIX! Extra effort from Gabriel and he oversteps. Then bowls a long hop, wide outside off. Shaw latches onto it and flays hard. Gets it over third man! The deficit is now 297.
A short leg comes in now. Short stuff or double bluff?
FOUR! Excellent shot to get off the mark! On a length outside off, Shaw leaps with the bounce and guides it behind gully to third man!
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, on a length, punched towards point.

Off the mark straightaway! Full and outside off, Rahul drives it through the covers. It is in the gap and Kieran Powell gets to it from mid off. Just about stops it near the ropes. Three runs taken. The deficit is now 308.
